ref_extractions.title: Age-Related Differences in Corticospinal Excitability during Observation and Motor Imagery of Balance Tasks
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper studies TMS-evoked MEPs during MI/AO of balance tasks in elderly vs young adults. It uses a completely different experimental setup (single-channel EMG/TMS, balance posture tasks) and does not reference or use the openneuro_ds007327 dataset which features sport-related ball passing/dribbling tasks with 88-channel EEG.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Separate TMS/EMG study on balance posture tasks; no dataset reference found.

ref_extractions.title: Experts Integrate Explicit Contextual Priors and Environmental Information to Improve Anticipation Efficiency
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper investigates Bayesian decision-making in soccer anticipation using gaze tracking. No EEG recording involved; it's purely behavioral/eye-tracking study with soccer video stimuli. Does not use the openneuro_ds007327 EEG dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Soccer anticipation behavioral study; no EEG data collected.

ref_extractions.title: Human electrocortical dynamics while stepping over obstacles
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper uses a custom dual-layer mobile EEG system during treadmill locomotion and obstacle stepping. The paradigm (walking/running with gait perturbations) is entirely different from the sport-related motor imagery and observation paradigm in openneuro_ds007327.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Mobile EEG locomotion study; not related to motor imagery/observation dataset.

ref_extractions.title: Prediction of Three-Dimensional Arm Trajectories Based on ECoG Signals Recorded from Human Sensorimotor Cortex
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper uses ECoG (intracranial EEG) from 3 patients performing 3D block repositioning tasks. It uses a fundamentally different recording modality (ECoG vs scalp EEG) and a different motor task paradigm. Does not reference openneuro_ds007327.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: ECoG study in patients; different modality and task from target dataset.

ref_extractions.title: Motion Artifact Removal Techniques for Wearable EEG and PPG Sensor Systems
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a review article surveying motion artifact removal techniques for wearable EEG and PPG devices. It does not analyze any specific EEG dataset or conduct experiments with openneuro_ds007327.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Review paper; no dataset analysis performed.

ref_extractions.title: Long-term asynchronous decoding of arm motion using electrocorticographic signals in monkeys
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper uses ECoG recordings from two monkeys performing asynchronous food-reaching tasks. Different modality (ECoG vs scalp EEG), different species (monkeys vs humans), and different behavioral paradigm. Does not use openneuro_ds007327.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Monkey ECoG study; different modality and subject species.

ref_extractions.title: Post-task Effects on EEG Brain Activity Differ for Various Differential Learning and Contextual Interference Protocols
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper examines EEG changes after badminton serve practice with different motor learning protocols. The study uses a 19-channel EEG system and analyzes post-task effects. It does not reference or use openneuro_ds007327, which focuses on motor imagery/observation during ball tasks.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Motor learning EEG study with badminton serves; different paradigm from MI/MO dataset.

ref_extractions.title: Brain Oscillations in Sport: Toward EEG Biomarkers of Performance
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a review article discussing EEG biomarkers across various sports including hockey, tennis, and golf. It does not present original experimental data from openneuro_ds007327. The paper is a general review/survey of EEG in sport contexts.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Review article on EEG in sport; no primary data analysis.

ref_extractions.title: A Review of Human Activity Recognition Methods
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a survey paper reviewing computer vision methods for human activity recognition from video. It discusses datasets but does not use or reference openneuro_ds007327, which is an EEG motor imagery dataset, not a video activity recognition dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Review of video-based activity recognition; no EEG dataset involved.

ref_extractions.title: Comparison of Smoothing Filters in Analysis of EEG Data for the Medical Diagnostics Purposes
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper compares smoothing filters (Savitzky-Golay, median) on EEG data for medical diagnostics using 4 channels (C3, C4, P3, P4). It does not use or reference openneuro_ds007327. The focus is on signal processing methodology, not motor imagery classification.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: EEG filtering methodology paper; no motor imagery dataset used.

ref_extractions.title: BioMove: Biometric User Identification from Human Kinesiological Movements for Virtual Reality Systems
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper proposes a biometric identification system using kinesiological movement data captured from VR devices (head, hand, eye tracking). No EEG signals are used; the approach is based on inertial/orientational sensors. Does not use openneuro_ds007327.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: VR kinesiology study; no EEG involved, different modality entirely.

feasibility_reason: This dataset is a public OpenNeuro repository with a well-documented 2x2 factorial motor imagery/observation paradigm containing 9 distinct event classes with clear label mappings. The analysis.md provides sufficient paradigm detail including epoch parameters (tmin=-0.2s, tmax=1.0s) and target event definitions to support motor intention/observation classification tasks. While no reference papers directly analyze this dataset, the comprehensive event structure and public dataset status satisfy feasibility criteria.

## Tasks

### Classical Task 1: 4-Class Motor Imagery/Observation Compound Classification
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = 0.0 s, tmax = 3.0 s, target_events = see Target Definition
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:

| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| B12 | 0 | Motor imagination x intention (Task B) |
| B14 | 1 | Motor imagination x observation (Task B) |
| B16 | 2 | Motor observation x intention (Task B) |
| B18 | 3 | Motor observation x observation (Task B) |

- **Evidence**: No direct DOI reference available. Task derived from paradigm description on official dataset page: https://openneuro.org/datasets/ds007327
- **Kernel Notes**: The A/B/C prefix in raw event IDs encodes the three task types per subject (ballpass/dribble/passing). The 4-class compound conditions (MIMI/MIMO/MOMI/MOMO) are represented by B12/B14/B16/B18 for Task B files and C12/C14/C16/C18 for Task C files (~4197 trials each). Verify exact mapping against events.tsv. Exclude B99/C99 (~19500 counts), B96/B98/C96/C98 (~2800 each), and A98/A99 (~2100/421) as administrative markers. Apply 88-channel exclusion mask to remove 24 BIP (EMG/kinematic) channels. Alignment assumed as CUE ONSET based on 'short' event classification (<2 s) and BCI-style paradigm structure.

### Classical Task 2: 9-Class Full Condition Classification
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 1.0 s, target_events = see Target Definition
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:

| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| A11 | 0 | Motor observation (Task A) |
| A22 | 1 | Motor intention (Task A) |
| A44 | 2 | Resting baseline (Task A) |
| A66 | 3 | Static baseline (Task A) |
| A88 | 4 | Motor observation with intention (Task A) |
| B12 | 5 | Motor imagination x intention (Task B) |
| B14 | 6 | Motor imagination x observation (Task B) |
| B16 | 7 | Motor observation x intention (Task B) |
| B18 | 8 | Motor observation x observation (Task B) |

- **Evidence**: No direct DOI reference available. Task derived from paradigm description on official dataset page: https://openneuro.org/datasets/ds007327
- **Kernel Notes**: This task includes all nine conditions (4 compound + 4 single-factor + baseline). Pre-stimulus baseline of 0.2 s enables baseline correction. Exclude administrative markers (B99, B96, B98, C99, C96, C98, A98, A99, Impedance, boundary). Apply channel exclusion mask for 24 BIP channels. Verify event-to-condition mapping against events.tsv. Task A files contain single-factor conditions (A11/A22/A44/A66/A88); Task B/C files contain compound conditions. Filter by file/task prefix before assigning labels.

### Potential Task 1: Rest vs Active Binary Classification
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = 0.0 s, tmax = 3.0 s, target_events = see Target Definition
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:

| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| A44 | 0 | Resting baseline (negative class) |
| A66 | 0 | Static baseline (negative class) |
| A11 | 1 | Motor observation (positive class) |
| A22 | 1 | Motor intention (positive class) |
| A88 | 1 | Motor observation with intention (positive class) |
| B12 | 1 | Motor imagination x intention (positive class) |
| B14 | 1 | Motor imagination x observation (positive class) |
| B16 | 1 | Motor observation x intention (positive class) |
| B18 | 1 | Motor observation x observation (positive class) |

- **Evidence**: Plausible from paradigm alone (binary baseline contrast for ERD/ERS detection); no DOI reference required.
- **Kernel Notes**: Binary contrast of rest/static baseline against any active motor condition. Useful for detecting motor-related spectral perturbations. Use same tmax=3.0 s as active conditions for balanced epoch lengths. Exclude all administrative markers (B99, B96, B98, C99, C96, C98, A98, A99, Impedance, boundary). Apply channel exclusion mask for 24 BIP channels. Kernel must pool single-factor (Task A) and compound (Task B/C) active events under label 1. Exclude Task C compound events or include based on analysis goals—verify against events.tsv.
